meta.description: Anima 2B LoRA, 5090 FAST profile: the performance preset plus every verified speed lever. gradient_checkpointing OFF (a 2B model on 32GB does not need the ~30-40% recompute tax), latents cached to disk AND served from RAM (cache_latents + cache_latents_to_disk — disk-only re-reads every step), text embeds cached (hard-unloads the text encoder), full bf16 no quantization, batch 2, samples/saves stretched to 500. Fork speed keys: loss_sync_every 4 (loss display/log updates every 4 steps instead of syncing the GPU every step), ui_db_poll_seconds 2 (UI stop/save/sample buttons take up to 2s to be noticed). Training math is identical to the performance preset — same effective batch 2, author's recipe (rank 32, AdamW 2e-5, LLM adapter frozen) apart from that batch, which this fork lowered from the author's 4 because effective batch 4 pushes the in-app step suggestion under its floor on small/medium datasets, where clamping inflates real per-image exposure into overfit range. If 1024 x batch 2 OOMs without checkpointing, drop batch_size to 1 before re-enabling gradient_checkpointing. Not for shared-GPU use — take the background preset for that. Effective batch 4 (batch 4 x accum 1) matches the Anima author's published recipe. Needs >=32 training files; below that use anima_background_gen_lora (effective batch 2). STEP TABLE (meta.step_table, 2026-10-12, machine-independent - the same table ships on every anima preset, laptop or desktop): 20 images ~1500, 30 images ~2250, 40 images ~3000, exact-count interpolation between rows, capped at 3000 steps. OPTIMIZED DATASET COUNT ~40 images: that is where the cap is reached; past it the panel keeps 3000 and the exposure gauge says the dataset is past the optimal size for this model and suggests curating down, instead of calling it undertrained. Source: the fork's Anima exposure target (75 steps/image, Anima-TrainFlow) - community Anima runs at LR 2e-5 report far more exposure (lilting.ch: 600-720 passes/image, i.e. ~12000 steps at 53 images), which does not transfer to these presets' higher LR, so the table caps at 3000. Values are steps at effective batch 1; the Step Suggestion panel divides by your effective batch (batch_size x gradient_accumulation), which is the only thing that differs between machines. Below the first row the first row's steps apply.
